heroHeadline: China's Big Fund Leads DeepSeek's First External Funding at $45B Valuation; MIIT Issues Internal 70% Domestic Silicon Wafer Mandate for 2026 Chipmakers
heroSubtitle: China's state-backed National IC Investment Fund (Big Fund) is leading DeepSeek's first external funding round at a $45 billion valuation (Bloomberg/FT, May 6–7), formally anchoring China's most consequential AI lab within the same state investment apparatus that built the domestic semiconductor supply chain. The $45 billion valuation — up from $20B+ estimates just weeks earlier — places DeepSeek above Mistral AI and near Anthropic in global AI startup rankings, and marks Beijing's explicit designation of DeepSeek as a national AI champion alongside its existing semiconductor investments. Tencent and Alibaba are also in talks to join the round. Separately, Nikkei Asia (May 5) published an exclusive revealing MIIT issued an internal directive requiring Chinese chipmakers to source 70% of silicon wafers domestically by end-2026 — extending China's self-sufficiency mandate to the foundational material layer of chip manufacturing, alongside the parallel 50% domestic equipment mandate for new fab capacity documented by Tom's Hardware. China's 15th Five-Year Plan has also elevated AI-powered robots to a core national industrial strategy: China operates 2 million industrial robots (54% of global annual installations), domestic supplier share rose from 30% to 57% in 2024, and ByteDance Doubao AI models are being integrated into robot control systems. Structural picture as of May 7, 2026: China's Big Fund now bridges semiconductor hardware (SMIC, YMTC, HiSilicon/Ascend chip program) and AI model software (DeepSeek V4) under the same state investment structure; MIIT is simultaneously mandating domestic wafers and equipment in fabs; Huawei commands ~60% of China's domestic AI chip market ($12B revenue forecast, +60% YoY); the Arena benchmark gap to US frontier AI models has narrowed to 39 points (2.7%); and China's tech stock benchmark hit an all-time record high on May 6. Every layer of the AI technology stack — chips, models, capital, wafers, equipment, robotics, physical deployment — is now being systematically localized under an integrated national strategy.
